visitSetup: Print one host guide, six visit format cards, a postcard stack, and extra blank half-sheets before the visit table opens.
Place pencils, object choice slips, pretend place strips, and plain folders where the adult host can pass them out one step at a time.
Choose three ordinary object starters such as a button, spoon, seed packet, paper clip, teacup, or ribbon before the first story begins.
Prepare one quiet seat with a pencil, sketch space, and two simple choice strips for anyone who wants to join without speaking first.
Use color tabs, table symbols, or blank folders for sorting instead of personal labels.
Keep the kit screen-free by using only printed pages, spoken choices, sketches, pointing, and short written lines.
storyHosting: Open with an invented helper, a pretend place, and one ordinary object so the story starts in make-believe space.
Model one sample answer that is clearly invented, then invite writers to choose by pointing, sketching, dictating, or writing.
Move through the page in small cooperative steps: place, helper, object, small mix-up, next action, and calm ending.
Offer two adult-made choices when a writer pauses, and let the writer pick, change, combine, or invent a third option.
Keep sharing optional and focused on a title, object clue, sketch, or one invented sentence from the printed page.
Use gentle table language such as maker, guide, visitor, helper, messenger, keeper, or builder for every pretend role.
quietParticipation: Let a participant complete only one blank, circle one choice, or draw one clue and still count the page as finished.
Offer a silent postcard path where the writer fills the pretend place and object blanks before any table talk.
Allow an adult to write a dictated phrase while the writer chooses the words, points to options, or sketches the clue.
Accept a folded page, underlined word, or shown sketch as complete sharing when reading aloud is not preferred.
Keep a spare fresh page nearby so a writer can restart without explanation if the first idea feels too crowded.
Invite partners to trade only invented object ideas, not personal details, when they want a cooperative prompt.
noDataUse: This kit uses invented helpers, pretend places, and ordinary objects; private facts are not needed.
Keep every page offline, printable, and handled by the host, writer, or household after the visit.
Do not collect private identifiers, personal labels, personal timelines, or household details.
Organize pages with symbols, colors, or plain folders instead of person-specific sorting.
Send finished work home or let the writer keep it at the table; the host does not need to retain copies.
takeHomeHandoff: Send home one finished visit page plus one optional story postcard for another screen-free writing moment.
Mark one simple next step such as add a title, add one setting detail, add one object clue, or finish the ending.
Tell households the postcard can be completed by pointing, sketching, dictating, or writing one short line.
Keep home sharing optional and focused on the printed page, invented place, ordinary object, title, or calm ending.
Invite the writer to save unused postcards for another table visit without requiring any follow-up report.
packReset: Return unused format cards and postcards to the host folder before clearing pencils and choice strips.
Place finished pages in plain take-home folders or let writers carry their own pages.
Restock blank pages, sharpen pencils, and replace bent choice strips before the next visit table.
Move used sample slips behind the host guide so the next host can begin with a fresh top card.
Write only a nonpersonal supply note if needed, such as more pencils, fewer object slips, or extra quiet pages.

visitFormats.name: Teacup Map Story
visitFormats.bestFor: A cozy table visit where an adult host and writer want a pretend place before the first sentence.
steps: Host places one teacup, button, or paper circle on the table and asks for a pretend place it could mark: ____________________.
Writer adds an invented helper who visits that place for a small friendly errand: ____________________.
Host offers two object choices and the writer picks one to become the clue: ____________________.
Together they write one opening sentence and circle the detail to keep: ____________________.

visitFormats.name: Button Messenger Visit
visitFormats.bestFor: Grandparent-style visits, neighbor-helper tables, and co-op family days with gentle back-and-forth writing.
steps: Host gives the writer a button card and asks what pretend message it carries: ____________________.
Writer chooses an invented messenger role such as guide, maker, keeper, or builder: ____________________.
Host asks where the messenger should deliver the object in a pretend town: ____________________.
Together they write the next action and leave the ending blank for later: ____________________.

visitFormats.name: Kitchen Drawer Quest
visitFormats.bestFor: Library family visit tables that need familiar object choices and no special supplies.
steps: Host spreads three printed object slips from an imaginary kitchen drawer and asks the writer to choose one: ____________________.
Writer invents a tiny mix-up the object can help solve kindly: ____________________.
Host models one sentence using a different object so the writer can make a fresh choice: ____________________.
Writer adds first, next, and last story beats on the visit page: ____________________.

visitFormats.name: Porch Lantern Postcard
visitFormats.bestFor: A quieter visit where the writer wants a small postcard instead of a full page.
steps: Host points to the lantern picture space and asks what make-believe place it lights up: ____________________.
Writer sketches or writes one ordinary object waiting under the lantern: ____________________.
Host offers a calm helper choice and asks what the helper notices first: ____________________.
Writer completes one postcard line and chooses whether to share the title: ____________________.

visitFormats.name: Three-Chair Story Circle
visitFormats.bestFor: Homeschool co-op family days with one adult host and a small group of mixed-age writers.
steps: Host labels three chair spaces as place, object, and helper, then asks writers to fill the first blank: ____________________.
Each writer adds one invented object idea to the shared choice page: ____________________.
Host reads the choices aloud and lets each writer pick a different path for a private page: ____________________.
Writers finish with one calm ending line or one ending sketch: ____________________.

visitFormats.name: Tiny Shopkeeper Scene
visitFormats.bestFor: A playful adult-led visit with pretend places, ordinary supplies, and cooperative sentence building.
steps: Host names an imaginary tiny shop and asks the writer what useful object sits in the window: ____________________.
Writer invents a shopkeeper, helper, or visitor who needs that object for a kind task: ____________________.
Host asks what small mix-up happens when the object is used in a surprising way: ____________________.
Together they write one dialogue line and one next action: ____________________.

takeHomePostcards.title: Pretend Porch Place
takeHomePostcards.direction: Invent a porch, table, garden step, or window nook for a story scene: ____________________.
takeHomePostcards.familyLine: A grown-up can ask what the pretend place looks or sounds like: ____________________.

takeHomePostcards.title: Object With a Job
takeHomePostcards.direction: Choose one ordinary object and give it a useful job in the story: ____________________.
takeHomePostcards.familyLine: A grown-up can offer two possible jobs for the object here: ____________________.

takeHomePostcards.title: Invented Helper Card
takeHomePostcards.direction: Create an invented helper who solves a tiny friendly mix-up: ____________________.
takeHomePostcards.familyLine: A grown-up can ask what the helper tries first: ____________________.

takeHomePostcards.title: Button Trail
takeHomePostcards.direction: Write first, next, and last for a button that rolls through a pretend place: ____________________.
takeHomePostcards.familyLine: A grown-up can point to the step that should become a longer sentence: ____________________.

takeHomePostcards.title: Teacup Clue
takeHomePostcards.direction: Describe a tiny clue found beside a teacup in an invented room: ____________________.
takeHomePostcards.familyLine: A grown-up can ask which describing word makes the clue clearer: ____________________.

takeHomePostcards.title: Window Nook Dialogue
takeHomePostcards.direction: Write two short lines between an invented guide and an invented visitor: ____________________.
takeHomePostcards.familyLine: A grown-up can read one role while the writer chooses the reply: ____________________.

takeHomePostcards.title: Shelf of Surprises
takeHomePostcards.direction: List three ordinary shelf objects that could start a make-believe scene: ____________________.
takeHomePostcards.familyLine: A grown-up can choose one object and ask what changes when it moves: ____________________.

takeHomePostcards.title: Kind Ending
takeHomePostcards.direction: Add a calm ending where the helper uses one object wisely: ____________________.
takeHomePostcards.familyLine: A grown-up can ask what feels settled at the end: ____________________.

takeHomePostcards.title: Tiny Map Mark
takeHomePostcards.direction: Draw or describe one mark on a pretend map and explain why it matters: ____________________.
takeHomePostcards.familyLine: A grown-up can ask where the helper should go next: ____________________.

takeHomePostcards.title: Clearer Word Swap
takeHomePostcards.direction: Pick one plain word from the visit page and swap in a clearer word: ____________________.
takeHomePostcards.familyLine: A grown-up can ask which word is easier to picture now: ____________________.

takeHomePostcards.title: Sketch Then Sentence
takeHomePostcards.direction: Sketch one story object and write one sentence under it: ____________________.
takeHomePostcards.familyLine: A grown-up can ask which part of the sketch belongs in the story: ____________________.

takeHomePostcards.title: Next Visit Seed
takeHomePostcards.direction: Invent one pretend place, one helper, one object, and one small mix-up for next time: ____________________.
takeHomePostcards.familyLine: A grown-up can add one extra make-believe detail to the seed: ____________________.

optionalFamilySharePrompts: Show one invented place from the visit page: ____________________.
Read one sentence aloud, or ask a grown-up to read it: ____________________.
Point to one ordinary object and tell how it helps the helper: ____________________.
Share one title choice for the postcard story: ____________________.
Tell which story step came first, next, or last: ____________________.
Show one sketch and name the invented clue inside it: ____________________.
Describe one calm ending choice from the make-believe story: ____________________.
Keep the page private today and mark one finished detail: ____________________.
